title: Which WordprocessingML constructs the LastWord document model can express, and the exact XML each one emits

contract.summary: LastWord's three engines (PHP, Node, Python) turn one JSON document model into .docx. This suite pins the MAPPING: for a given model fragment, which property elements land in word/document.xml, with which attributes, in which order — and whether the reader gives the model back. It exists because the model was far narrower than the XML the writers emit: font size, font family, small caps, letter spacing, per-cell shading, borders, padding, vertical alignment and both merge directions were emitted from hardcoded blocks or styles.xml and were unreachable from the model. An agent could emit them, the validator returned no errors, and all three engines silently dropped them.

functions.runProps: write the doc, unzip, parse word/document.xml, and return every <w:r> in body order as {text, rPr} where rPr is the ordered normalisation of that run's properties.
functions.paragraphProps: …every <w:p> in body order as the ordered normalisation of its <w:pPr> (an empty array when absent).
functions.tableProps: …every <w:tbl> in body order as {tblPr, grid} — tblPr ordered-normalised, grid the list of <w:gridCol w:w> values as strings.
functions.cellProps: …every <w:tc> in document order as the ordered normalisation of its <w:tcPr>.
functions.footnotesPart: write the doc, unzip, and return {contentType, relationship, footnotePr, references, footnotes}: contentType is the ContentType of the [Content_Types].xml Override for /word/footnotes.xml (null when absent); relationship is the Target of the word/_rels/document.xml.rels Relationship whose Type ends /footnotes (null when absent); footnotePr is the ordered normalisation of <w:footnotePr> in word/settings.xml (null when there is no settings part or no footnotePr); references is the w:id of every <w:footnoteReference> in word/document.xml in document order, as strings; footnotes is every <w:footnote> child of word/footnotes.xml in order (empty when there is no part) as {id, type, text, content}: id the w:id string, type the w:type string or null when absent, text the concatenated text of every <w:t> in it, content the ordered normalisation of the <w:footnote> element itself (recursive: an element with element children is [name, normalisation of its children]). Attribute names are local names, so xml:space is "space".
functions.bandParts: write the doc and return {titlePg, evenAndOddHeaders, references, parts}: titlePg is whether the body's <w:sectPr> has a <w:titlePg> child; evenAndOddHeaders whether word/settings.xml has a <w:evenAndOddHeaders> child (false without a settings part); references is every <w:headerReference> / <w:footerReference> of that sectPr in order as {kind, type, target, text}: kind "header" or "footer", type the w:type string, target the Target of the word/_rels/document.xml.rels Relationship its r:id names, text the concatenated text of every <w:t> in that part (the cached results of its fields included); parts is the sorted list of every archive entry matching word/header*.xml or word/footer*.xml.
functions.bandFields: write the doc and, for each header/footer part the body's sectPr references, in reference order and once per target, return {target, fields}: fields is every complex field in the part in document order as {instruction, result}, instruction the concatenated <w:instrText> between its begin and separate <w:fldChar> (spaces kept), result the concatenated <w:t> text between separate and end ("" when there is no result run).
functions.coreProps: write the doc; null when there is no docProps/core.xml; otherwise {contentType, relationship, elements}: contentType the ContentType of the [Content_Types].xml Override for /docProps/core.xml (null when absent), relationship the Target of the _rels/.rels Relationship whose Type ends /core-properties (null when absent), elements every child element of cp:coreProperties in order as [qualified name, text content], e.g. ["dc:title", "Board memo"].
functions.sections: write the doc and return every <w:sectPr> of word/document.xml in document order, paragraph-borne ones first and the body's own last, each as {props, references}: props the ordered normalisation of the sectPr without its header and footer references; references those references in order as {kind, type, target, tabs}: target the part name its relationship names, tabs the w:pos of every <w:tab> in that part's first <w:tabs>, as strings ([] when it has none).
functions.readFile: read(fixtureBytes(input.file)): the document model recovered from a file this package did not write. input.file is a file reference.
functions.readBack: read(toBytes(doc)) — the document model recovered from the bytes just written.
functions.roundTripFixpoint: {"fixpoint": read(toBytes(doc)) == doc}. Proves the reader is complete for every construct the writer emits, without a golden the size of the document.

runShape.rowInput: Since 0.41.0 every function takes the row's whole input, {doc, template?, options?}. doc is the document model. template, when present, is ITSELF a document model: the engine writes it with toBytes() and passes those bytes as the template write option. options, when present, are further write options passed as given (templateParts, templateFirstPageOnly). Rows before 0054 carry doc alone, and write it with no options, exactly as before.
runShape.normalisedProps: An ORDERED array of [localName, value] pairs, one per child element of the property container. value is `true` for an empty element, an object of attribute-localName -> string for an element with attributes, and a nested ordered array for an element with element children. Attribute values are ALWAYS strings, so no language's number parsing can enter the comparison.

contract.referenceNote: particle-academy/last-word is the reference: it shipped first and the pair's contract is 'same document either backend'. Two exceptions are recorded in `notes` — the header-cell grey and the table property block — where the reference was reconciled TOWARD the Node port rather than the other way, because the port's value was the considered one. Every golden here is the output of running an engine after that reconciliation, never what the XML 'obviously' ought to be; the unit arithmetic (points to half-points, points to twentieths, points to eighths) is stated in the notes so a reader can check a row rather than trust it.

notes: ORDER IS THE POINT. WordprocessingML fixes the child order of every property container (CT_RPr, CT_PPr, CT_TcPr, CT_TblPr, CT_SectPr are xsd:sequence, not xsd:all), so a normalisation to an unordered map would let two engines emit different XML and still pass. The goldens are ordered arrays for that reason, and three rows exist only to pin an insertion point - 0006, 0014, 0031. Attribute order WITHIN an element is deliberately NOT pinned, because attributes are unordered in XML; pinning it is a byte-level parts comparison, which is the binary suite's job rather than this one's.

UNIT ARITHMETIC, stated once so every row is checkable rather than believable. Font size: points -> HALF-points (w:sz = pt*2). Letter spacing, paragraph spacing, indents and cell margins: points -> TWENTIETHS of a point (twips, = pt*20). Border width: points -> EIGHTHS of a point (w:sz = pt*8, clamped to OOXML's 2..96). Table width: percent -> FIFTIETHS of a percent (w:w = pct*50, w:type=pct). Line height: a multiple -> w:line = mult*240 with w:lineRule=auto. Column widths are relative WEIGHTS normalised over the section's content width, so [30,40,30] and [3,4,3] are the same table.

THE GRID DEPENDS ON THE PAGE. Column widths are computed against page width minus the two side margins, so a document that narrows its margins gets a wider grid. Case 0032 pins that link; before this suite the content width was the constant 9360 in all three engines and a custom margin silently produced a table narrower or wider than its own page.

RECONCILED, NOT DISCOVERED. Three divergences between the engines were live when this suite was written and are fixed by the same change that adds these rows, so the goldens are what all three now emit: (a) Node referenced a shared <w:tblStyle w:val="LastWordTable"/> while PHP and Python inlined <w:tblBorders> — a named style cannot vary per table instance, so per-table borders forced inlining everywhere; (b) header cells were E7E7E7 in PHP and Python but F2F2F2 in Node — two greys for one input; (c) PHP and Python wrote <w:b/> onto header runs while Node got bold from <w:tblStylePr w:type="firstRow">, so the same file read back to two different models depending on which engine wrote it. Node moved to the majority on (b) and (c); all three moved to Node's more generous default cell margins when its style was inlined.

NO ROW ASSERTS A COLOUR IS PRETTY. Every golden here is a mapping fact. Whether a document built from these constructs LOOKS like anything is not a fixture's business, and is checked by rendering the reference document in case 0039 and looking at it.

FOOTNOTES (0.40.0, rows 0045-0050). A footnote is a RUN, {"text": "", "footnote": {"blocks": [...]}}, placed where the mark goes; the model carries no number, Word numbers the marks in document order. The writer numbers footnotes 1, 2, 3 as their runs render (body order, depth-first through tables, lists and quotes), writes the separator (w:id -1) and continuation separator (w:id 0) Word requires, names them in settings <w:footnotePr>, and adds the FootnoteText / FootnoteReference styles only when a footnote exists. A footnote's blocks render through the body's block renderer against the footnotes part's OWN relationships (word/_rels/footnotes.xml.rels). The reader strips the one space that follows a footnote's own <w:footnoteRef/> and never merges or drops a footnote run. Not in a header or footer, and never one inside another: validation refuses both and the writer writes nothing for them.

PAGE GEOMETRY (0.40.0, rows 0051-0053). page.margins gains header and footer, the w:pgMar distances from the page edge to the header and to the footer, in points (twips = pt*20 on the wire). The reader keeps its rule that a value equal to the writer's default is OMITTED (1440 twips = 72pt per side, 720 twips = 36pt per distance), and omits page entirely when nothing differs, so no existing read output changed. A consumer resolves an absent value as that default; PHP exposes it as Schema::pageMargins().

FIRST-PAGE LETTERHEAD (0.41.0, rows 0054-0060). The write option templateFirstPageOnly (boolean, default false) carries the template's header and footer -- those templateParts names -- as Word's FIRST-page parts only, with w:titlePg on: the template's own first-page part when its titlePg is on and it has one, else its default part; never its even part, and no w:evenAndOddHeaders. Each carried part is word/{kind}4.xml with relationship id rIdTpl{Kind}4, because numbers 1-3 are the document's own bands by slot and can sit beside it. Later pages get the document's page.header / page.footer, or nothing. A document firstHeader (firstFooter) wins over the template's for that kind; nothing else does. false and absent are identical, byte for byte.

FIRST AND EVEN BANDS (0.41.0, rows 0061-0066). page.firstHeader / firstFooter / evenHeader / evenFooter, each the shape of page.header (a slot band or a blocks band). The document's own parts are numbered by SLOT: {kind}1.xml default (rId{Kind}1, unchanged), {kind}2.xml first (rId{Kind}2), {kind}3.xml even (rId{Kind}3), rendered header before footer and default, first, even within a kind (which fixes media numbering). A first band turns w:titlePg on (last child of sectPr); an even band writes w:evenAndOddHeaders in settings.xml. With a switch on, a kind that has a default part and no variant references its default for those pages too. References are written default, first, even within a kind, header before footer -- except a kind taken whole from a template without templateFirstPageOnly, which keeps the template's own references in its own order, byte for byte. An EMPTY variant ({"blocks": []}, or a band with no text) is an empty part (one <w:p/>) when the document's own default band of that kind exists, and nothing otherwise. read() returns a first (even) variant only while w:titlePg (w:evenAndOddHeaders) is on, skips one naming the same part as the default, and returns {"blocks": []} for a missing or empty variant part while the default has content.

FIELD TOKENS (0.41.0, rows 0067-0074). In header and footer text -- band slots and a blocks band's run text, never the body -- these are live COMPLEX fields: {page} PAGE, {pages} NUMPAGES, {section} SECTION, {sectionpages} SECTIONPAGES, {author} AUTHOR, {title} TITLE, {filename} FILENAME, {date} DATE, {time} TIME, and {date:FORMAT} / {time:FORMAT} as DATE \@ "FORMAT" / TIME \@ "FORMAT". FORMAT is a Word date-time picture of one or more characters, none of {, }, " or a backslash; names are lower-case and exact; anything else in braces is literal text. Each field is begin / instrText " INSTRUCTION " / separate / result / end, every piece a run in the band's formatting. The cached RESULT is deterministic: "1" for PAGE, NUMPAGES, SECTION and SECTIONPAGES; meta.author for AUTHOR and the document title for TITLE ("" without one); no result run for DATE, TIME and FILENAME. The reader maps any producer's field to its token by its first word, any case, keeping a DATE / TIME \@ picture the grammar can hold and dropping every other switch and argument; SECTIONPAGES now reads as {sectionpages} (it read as {pages} before 0.41.0), and a field that is not a token keeps its cached result as text in a one-line band as it already did in a blocks band.

MIXED PAGES (0.45.0, rows 0080-0092). A pageBreak carrying page starts a new Word section. Each section's w:sectPr goes in a dedicated empty paragraph after its last block, the body's own being the last section's, with no w:br and no w:type (absent is nextPage). Each text width gets its own header and footer parts, because a one-line band hard-codes its tab stops; the first stretch keeps {kind}1-{kind}3 by slot and later parts number from 5, shared only between stretches whose band was set in the same place and whose text is the same width, and never for a band holding {section}, whose cached result is its number. titlePg is per section, evenAndOddHeaders per document; a later section names a blank part for a band it does not show, because Word inherits a reference left out. read() gives top-level page from the FIRST section and each later one as a break holding what differs; 0091 and 0092 are files this package did not write, with sectPr where Word puts it and w:type in use. The stretch rules are fine-print's: margins merge side by side, every other key is replaced whole, firstHeader and firstFooter are never inherited.

META (0.41.0, rows 0075-0079). meta.author is docProps/core.xml dc:creator, written after dc:title; a core part is written when the document has a title or a non-empty author, and a title-only part is unchanged. The title remains the top-level title: there is deliberately no meta.title, so dc:title has one slot. read() returns meta: {author} right after title, only for a non-empty dc:creator.

Case 0039 carries a whole business one-pager as its input — a KPI band, a dark full-bleed callout, a bordered grid with one tinted cell, a card row, a definition table with a tinted label column and a two-tint closing pair. It is the acceptance artifact for the capability, reduced here to the one claim a fixture can make about it: everything the writer emitted, the reader gave back. Its content is neutral and invented; it reproduces the STRUCTURE of a real client document and none of its text, names or branding.
